evidence: Traupman 57: ossa frangere, to break bones

phrases.latin: Bracchium frāctum est; medicus id dēligābit.
phrases.english: The arm is broken; the doctor will bandage it up.

phrases.latin: excūsāvit Vespa Terentius, quod eum bracchium frēgisse dīceret
phrases.english: Vespa Terentius made his excuses for him, saying he had broken his arm

phrases.latin: ait sē obligāsse crūs frāctum Aesculāpiō, Apollinī autem brachium
phrases.english: he says he has set a broken leg for Aesculapius, and an arm for Apollo (a doctor mending statues)

sources: Lewis & Short: fractura · Lewis & Short: obligo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 57, 64.
